title: Your Personal Open-Source Humanoid Robot for $8,999 — JX Mo, K-Scale Labs
talk_summary: A founding engineer at K-Scale Labs presents their open-source humanoid robots (Kbot and Zbot), emphasizing a fully open hardware/software/ML stack, a simple Python/Rust SDK, and a simulation digital twin with the same gRPC interface as the real robot so code transfers by changing an IP address. They attribute their small team's velocity to open-source community bounties, hackathons, and a modular, minimal-complexity design.

takeaways.technique: Sim/real parity via identical interface and IP swap
takeaways.what_they_do: Their simulation (ksim) exposes the same gRPC interface as the physical robot, so the only change between prototyping in sim and deploying to hardware is the IP address.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all you have to do between programming something in simulation and real is by changing the IP address

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately skipped ROS/ROS2 because their robot has few sensors and is policy-based, choosing a simple Python/Rust SDK installable via pip instead of a complex async node ecosystem.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we really don't have that many sensors and we really want to do this like model based like policy based robot

takeaways.what_they_do: A 15-person team scales output by posting public open bounties on their MIT-licensed codebase and running bi-monthly hackathons, letting the community take discrete tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have a lot of public open bounties that people are tackling

takeaways.what_they_do: Training a walking policy takes 1-2 hours, results are watched in TensorBoard, then evaluated in simulation before deployment; they claim ~10x faster setup than typical training libraries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: training a walking policy roughly takes one hour to uh two hours
takeaways.numbers: 1-2 hours per policy; ~500 lines of training code; ~10x faster setup claim
